_meta: A short list of sensor readings with one MISSING value, used to show why NaN (not-a-number, the IEEE-754 float that represents a missing or undefined result) breaks every operation that relies on equality or ordering. readings_raw is the fixture: numbers plus a null marking the one missing reading, which the code turns into float('nan'). NaN has one defining, surprising property: it does not equal itself (nan == nan is False, nan != nan is True), and every ordered comparison with it (<, <=, >, >=) is also False. That single fact silently breaks four common operations: detecting the missing value by equality (x == nan never matches, so a naive filter misses it), sorting (comparisons with nan are all False, so sorted() returns a list that is not actually ordered -- with the readings 2, 3, missing, 1 the sort leaves the 1 stranded at the end, after the 3), and summing or averaging (any arithmetic involving nan yields nan, contaminating the whole result). The portable fix is to test for NaN with math.isnan (or the equivalent x != x, true ONLY for NaN), filter it out first, then compute on the clean values -- here mean = (2+3+1)/3 = 2.0. readings_raw is the fixture; every detection, sort, sum, and clean statistic is computed.
